BLOCKER: `go/edpsvc/internal/observe/metrics.go`: after replacing `edp_store_latency_ms` with `ObserveHistogram`, the local `ms` and its negative clamp are left unused; Go rejects unused locals, so `go test ./...` cannot build.
`go/edpsvc/main.go` `cacheHandle`: `tenant` is required but never namespaces the key; `/admin/cache` GET/PUT/DELETE can read or overwrite another tenant’s cached bytes, bypassing tenant isolation.
MAJOR: `main.go`: any error from `degrade.NewPolicy` — including invalid `config/edp-degradation.json` — is swallowed and replaced by an empty policy instead of startup refusal, violating `CONFIG_INVALID` and fail-closed behavior.
`degrade/policy.go`: the new renewal counter is only returned by unused `RenewalCount`; no metric/alert/bound is emitted, so degradation can be renewed indefinitely without detection.
`cache/memory.go` + `main.go`: the store has no capacity/eviction bound and the handler always calls `Set` with `ttl=0`; the admin cache can grow without limit and never expires.
`bench/slo.go`: for `MaxError > 0`, any scenario with `Err != ""` is accepted, so a positive `max_errors` disables all error violations rather than bounding counts.

`scripts/dev/db_explain_capture.py`: `--state`/`--audit` are optional, the rate check is non-atomic, and there is no concurrency cap; the required per-minute/concurrency/audit guarantees remain bypassable.
`main.go` object store: quota is only reached via `/admin/object-store/conform` with `tenant=""`, so `Quota` is skipped for object store and real object operations remain unguarded.
MINOR: `db_explain_capture.py`: `rate_ok` consumes a slot even when sampling later skips the run, causing false `REFUSE` under normal sampled-out traffic.
`degrade/policy.go`: `Policy.Check` takes a global mutex and `os.Stat`s the config on every store operation, serializing hot-path calls and adding filesystem I/O.
`storeguard/guard.go`: `Do` checks only `g == nil`, not `g.Degrade`; a zero-value `Guard` panics instead of failing safe.
`validate_edp_slo.py`: sibling `import gen_edp_slo` inside `problems()` depends on `sys.path`; imported-module/pytest execution can fail with `ModuleNotFoundError`.
`validate_edp_slo.py`: alert presence is checked by substring, not exact rule/alert name, so a summary or comment can satisfy the check.
NIT: `db_explain_capture.py`: state/audit file opens are not context-managed; state writes are not atomic.
`audit` records are append-only with no rotation/fsync/retention enforcement in the tool.
`gen_edp_slo.py` hardcodes non-benchmark alerts while `validate_edp_slo.py` separately hardcodes required names; generation and validation can drift in the non-generated portion.
SUMMARY: The delta fixes several prior gaps (generated SLO rules, store guard wiring, histogram metrics, baseline references) but introduces a build blocker and a tenant-isolation bug in the new admin cache.
Remaining enterprise risks: silent degradation-config fallback, unbounded cache, incomplete `max_errors` semantics, and EXPLAIN controls that remain optional/non-atomic.
AC-4 per-store quota is not demonstrated for object store; the only object guard path skips quota with an empty tenant.
Blockers must be fixed before merge; majors should be fixed or explicitly accepted with runbook controls.
